findings.title: Spawned workers fail the process type check and are never killed on restart
findings.body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose SpawnProcess class is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process. Consequently, this isinstance check is false for production workers and process.kill() is skipped. When a worker hangs, its replacement starts while the original remains alive and shares the same health and backpressure values. If the original resumes, both workers can flush the same shards concurrently, risking duplicate production and incorrect health reporting. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or otherwise distinguish workers from test threads, and exercise restart behavior with a real spawned process.

findings.title: Do not skip remaining workers when the shutdown deadline expires
findings.body: When the shared join deadline expires, this break skips cleanup for the current worker and every remaining worker. A worker blocked in Redis or waiting for Kafka delivery can therefore survive join(), including across partition reassignment, while its process handle is abandoned with the old strategy. The stopped flag does not interrupt those blocking operations. Apply the deadline only to graceful waiting, then terminate and reap every remaining process rather than breaking out of the cleanup loop.
